body: @iocanel @maxandersen have you seen this kind of discrepancy between OCP 3.11 and 4.x?
I haven't tried that specific setup in 3.11 - surprised there would be a difference here though...

That's weird. This is something that we do test.
I am wondering if the problem lies in `DB_PASSWORD` and how the quarkus config framework handles capitals and/or underscores.
Do you plan to check it out @iocanel ?

I think that the problem here lies in the expectation. 

While the quarkus kubernetes extension does support passing environment variables from secret, it doesn't provide fine-grained control. This means that the whole secret is passed instead of adding property by property.

So the following configuration:

```
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_DATABASE.secret=postgresql
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_DATABASE.value=database
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_USERNAME.secret=postgresql
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_USERNAME.value=username
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_PASSWORD.secret=postgresql
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_PASSWORD.value=password
```

could be replaced with:

```
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.THIS_IS_IGNORED.secret=postgresql
```

Or using the new style:

```
quarkus.kubernetes.env.secrets=postgresql
```

@iocanel Thanks for looking into this. 

I still don't see `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME` or `DB_PASSWORD` on OCP3.11 holding the secret, though. The values respectively are `database`, `username` and `password`. If I remove the `*.value=*` lines from yaml, the environment variables are not exported at all. Shouldn't the contain the secret?

Is it possible to configure the export of single key/value pair into an environment variable in `application.properties`? How would the example above look, if it was?

Is the secrets being exported as the vars just a fluke on OCP4 side?

> @iocanel Thanks for looking into this.
> 
> I still don't see `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME` or `DB_PASSWORD` on OCP3.11 holding the secret, though. The values respectively are `database`, `username` and `password`. If I remove the `*.value=*` lines from yaml, the environment variables are not exported at all. Shouldn't the contain the secret?

By having just:

```
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.THIS_IS_IGNORED.secret=postgresql

```

or 

```
quarkus.kubernetes.env.secrets=postgresql
```

The generated YAML will contain:

```
       envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: postgresql
```

And yes, this doesn't allow you to do any sort of mapping, like: `database -> DB_DATABASE`. The environment variable will be named `database` or whatever is the entry in your secret.

> 
> Is it possible to configure the export of single key/value pair into an environment variable in `application.properties`? How would the example above look, if it was?

If you mean to just add a single key/value pair from the secret, then no, its not possible ATM!

> Is the secrets being exported as the vars just a fluke on OCP4 side?

The generator is unaware of your cluster version. The generated yaml, is expected to be the same regardless of the target cluster, it something that can work even offline.

issue.title: Environment variables from secrets are not exported on OCP 3.11
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Exporting secrets as environment variables as described by [Deploying to OpenShift guide](https://quarkus.io/guides/deploying-to-openshift#environment-variables-from-secret) does not work on OCP 3.11.

The same feature works correctly on OCP 4.x.

**Expected behavior**
Secrets should be present in environment variables specified by the property name.

**Actual behavior**
Environment variables are not available in deployment pods on OCP 3.11.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Checkout https://github.com/mjurc/mock-artifacts  
2. `oc login` to OCP 3.11
3. `cd quarkus/getting-started/`
4. `oc apply -f src/main/resources/secret.yaml`
5. `mvn clean package`
6. check the deployment pod's env vars - the environment variables are not exported in environment variables as defined by the application's `application.properties` file, e. g. `DB_DATABASE=postgresql`

**Configuration**
```properties
quarkus.openshift.expose=true
quarkus.kubernetes-client.trust-certs=true
quarkus.s2i.base-jvm-image=registry.access.redhat.com/openjdk/openjdk-11-rhel7

quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_DATABASE.secret=postgresql
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_DATABASE.value=database
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_USERNAME.secret=postgresql
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_USERNAME.value=username
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_PASSWORD.secret=postgresql
quarkus.openshift.env-vars.DB_PASSWORD.value=password
```

body:
@iocanel Alright, I believe I found out what's the problem. As you said, Quarkus does not know about where it is going to be deployed. The `env` section from generated `kubernetes.yaml` is as follows:

```
      - env:
        - name: "KUBERNETES_NAMESPACE"
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: "metadata.namespace"
        - name: "DB_DATABASE"
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: "database"
              name: "postgresql"
              optional: false
        - name: "DB_PASSWORD"
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: "password"
              name: "postgresql"
              optional: false
        - name: "DB_USERNAME"
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: "username"
              name: "postgresql"
              optional: false
```
`secretKeyRef` does not have `optional` field on OCP 3.11 as far as I can see - and if the `optional` field is present, the secret does not get imported to any environment variable whatsoever.

If the `optional` fields are removed, the secrets are exported properly.
@iocanel I am little confused on what the action item is on our side for this. Can you elaborate please?
